reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a real Hilbert space with its Borel σ-algebra, let μ be a measure on E, and let f:E→ℝ be twice continuously differentiable. Assume f and ∇f are square-integrable with respect to μ and x↦h(f(x)²) is μ-integrable, where h(t)=t log t for t>0 and h(0)=0. Let χ_R be the prescribed radial smooth cutoff, valued in [0,1], equal to one for ‖x‖≤R and zero for ‖x‖>2R. For n∈ℕ set f_n(x)=χ_{n+1}(x)f(x). Then, as n→∞, ∫_E f_n² dμ→∫_E f² dμ, ∫_E h(f_n²) dμ→∫_E h(f²) dμ, and ∫_E ‖∇f_n‖² dμ→∫_E ‖∇f‖² dμ.
objects: The measure μ, the scalar function f and its E-valued gradient, the specified cutoff χ_R and products f_n, and the three real integrals of the square, the square times its logarithm, and the squared gradient norm.
domains: E is a complete real inner-product space with the Borel σ-algebra. The functions f and f_n are real-valued on E; their gradients take values in E. All integrals are over E with respect to μ, and n ranges over ℕ.
quantifiers: For every such E, every measure μ on E, and every f:E→ℝ satisfying the hypotheses, all three asserted real limits hold as the natural-number index tends to infinity.
assumptions: f is C², f belongs to L²(μ), ∇f belongs to L²(μ;E), and f² log(f²) is μ-integrable with the value zero at f=0. There is no finite-dimensionality, finiteness-of-measure, or probability normalization hypothesis.
conclusion: The integrals of f_n², f_n² log(f_n²), and ‖∇f_n‖² converge to the corresponding integrals for f.
scopes: The single sequence f_n(x)=χ_{n+1}(x)f(x) is defined after fixing μ and f, and is used in all three conjuncts. The third integrand uses the gradient of the product f_n. These are limits of real integrals, not assertions of pointwise or norm convergence of functions.
constant_dependencies: The inner and outer cutoff radii are n+1 and 2(n+1), respectively, and depend only on n. The limits involve no free comparison constant and no claimed convergence rate.
